what: The describe (`described_memo`) could not be looked up in another database because three things a lookup needs were private to one crate or one process: the type and id codec that already writes values by content (`hir_ty::check_cache::ids`, pub(crate) and tied to one crate`s portable table), the units as a place in a process list (`Facing::units`), and `Counted`, which the walk asks of a callee before its describe and which costs the callee`s optimized body. Finding that the codec existed took reading four files after first planning to write a second one.
whys: the codec was written for one consumer (a crate`s bodies part) and kept its item naming inside
nothing lists which persisted codecs exist, so the next record of types starts by not knowing there is one
rule one-concept-one-home is checked for types and paths, not for codecs
prevention: docs/v2/plan/design/data.md (or the `memory-and-data` skill) names the one codec for types and ids across databases (`hir_ty::check_cache::port` over `ids` and `next_solver::persist`) and says a new record of types uses it; done in this lane only as the module`s own doc.
